cell_types.name: Three germ layers (embryoid bodies / trilineage test)
cell_types.summary: Embryoid bodies are floating aggregates of pluripotent cells that differentiate spontaneously and yield a mixture of all three germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm), not mesoderm alone. They are used as the classic functional test of pluripotency for a new iPSC line and as the first step of many older directed-differentiation methods.
cell_types.maturation_note: Germ-layer transcripts are usually scored after roughly 1.5-2 weeks of spontaneous differentiation; cystic EBs and occasional beating areas appear later. Directed (monolayer) trilineage tests are faster but are mostly done with commercial kits.

morphology.endpoint: Round to irregular floating aggregates, some with fluid-filled cysts; after plating, EBs flatten into a heterogeneous outgrowth with neural-looking, epithelial and mesenchymal patches.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact, sharp-edged colonies at 60-80% confluence, ready to be lifted as clumps or single cells.

stages.label: Fresh aggregates
stages.look: Small, smooth, bright aggregates floating in low-attachment dishes or sitting one per well.

stages.label: Growing embryoid bodies
stages.look: Larger, darker spheres; some start to show a clear outer layer and internal cavities.

stages.label: Cystic / mixed EBs
stages.look: Heterogeneous bodies, some cystic and translucent, containing derivatives of all three germ layers.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should fall as EBs differentiate; persistent expression means poor differentiation.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Lost early during spontaneous differentiation.

markers.name: PAX6
markers.note: Neuroectoderm readout commonly used in trilineage panels.

markers.name: NEFL
markers.note: Ectoderm marker used in the original human EB paper (neurofilament 68 kDa).

markers.name: TUBB3
markers.note: Common ectoderm stain on plated EB outgrowths.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Early, transient mesoderm marker.

markers.name: HBZ
markers.note: Mesoderm (embryonic blood) marker used in the original human EB paper.

markers.name: ACTC1
markers.note: Marks cardiac muscle; reported in a pulsing EB in the original paper.

markers.name: ACTA2
markers.note: Common mesoderm stain on plated EBs.

markers.name: AFP
markers.note: Endoderm (yolk-sac / hepatic type) marker used in the original human EB paper.

markers.name: SOX17
markers.note: Endoderm readout in most trilineage panels.

functional_assays: Detection of all three germ layers by RT-qPCR or immunostaining
Spontaneous beating areas in some EBs
qc: Markers of ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm are all detectable and pluripotency markers fall relative to the starting culture

protocols.name: Feeder-free EBs in defined E8/E6 medium with PVA
protocols.principle: Cells from defined E8 cultures are lifted with EDTA and aggregated in E8 containing polyvinyl alcohol and ROCK inhibitor (self-aggregation, hanging drops or AggreWell), then left to differentiate spontaneously in E6, which is E8 without FGF2 and TGF-beta.

source.authors: Lin Y, Chen G
source.title: Embryoid body formation from human pluripotent stem cells in chemically defined E8 media

protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs on Matrigel or vitronectin in E8. Passage 1:3 or 1:4 two days before (day -2) with 10 µM Y-27632, change to E8 without inhibitor on day -1, and start at 60-80% confluence.

stages.name: Aggregate formation

factors.name: Y-27632
factors.role: ROCK inhibitor; protects dissociated cells (10 µM is the dose given for passaging; the EB step only says 'with ROCK inhibitor')

stages.feeding: No change; overnight
actions: Wash once and incubate in 0.5 mM EDTA/PBS: 3-5 min for self-aggregating clumps, 10-15 min for single cells
Self-aggregation: wash clumps off in E8/PVA with ROCK inhibitor and move one 10 cm dish into one 10 cm low-attachment dish (5 ml)
Hanging drop option: 2,000 cells in 20 µl drops on a dish lid
AggreWell-800 option: 1.5 x 10^6 cells per well (5,000 cells per microwell), spin 100 x g for 3 min
Incubate overnight at 37 °C
stages.checkpoint: Compact aggregates visible the next morning

stages.name: Spontaneous differentiation
stages.feeding: Change medium every 2 days
actions: Move EBs to low-attachment or poly-HEMA coated dishes
Tilt the dish 30-45° so EBs settle at one edge, remove most medium and replace with E6
Culture for 9-14 days
stages.checkpoint: EBs enlarge and become heterogeneous; assess germ-layer markers at the end

materials: Ultra-low attachment dishes or poly-HEMA (20 mg/ml in 95% ethanol) coated petri dishes
tips: Hanging drops or AggreWell give EBs of uniform size; self-aggregation is quickest but sizes vary
Use only the inner part of the timeline you need: many labs harvest RNA at about day 10-14

The human EB assay goes back to Itskovitz-Eldor et al. 2000 (Mol Med 6:88-95, PMID 10859025), who showed zeta-globin (mesoderm), neurofilament 68 kDa (ectoderm) and alpha-fetoprotein (endoderm) in suspension EBs from human ES cells

For one uniform EB per well, the spin-EB method (Ng et al. 2008, Nat Protoc 3:768-76, PMID 18451785, DOI 10.1038/nprot.2008.42) pellets a fixed number of single cells in round-bottom low-attachment 96-well plates in defined APEL medium; a 2020 protocol from the same lab (Nafria et al., PMID 33377024) uses roughly 5,000-6,000 cells per well
pitfalls: EBs stick to ordinary tissue-culture plastic; use low-attachment or poly-HEMA surfaces
Losing EBs during medium changes is the usual cause of low yield; let them settle first
unverified: The source page does not describe how germ layers are assessed; marker panel here comes from the other sources and general practice
ROCK inhibitor concentration during EB formation is not stated (10 µM is given for passaging)
No DOI is listed for this StemBook protocol; PMID 28211653 is the NCBI Bookshelf record matched by title in Europe PMC

Itskovitz-Eldor 2000 and Ng 2008 are not given as separate protocols because only their abstracts could be read (scanned PDF and paywall): their media, cell numbers, spin settings and day numbers are unconfirmed

cell_types.notes: This entry gives all three germ layers at once; it is filed under mesoderm only because the catalogue needs a single lineage. EB differentiation is qualitative and line-dependent. For a quantitative trilineage test most labs now use directed monolayer kits or scorecard-style qPCR panels.

cell_types.name: Primordial germ cell-like cells (hPGCLC)
cell_types.summary: Primordial germ cells are the embryonic founders of sperm and eggs, set aside around weeks 2-3 of human development. hPGCLCs made from iPSCs are used to study human germline specification, epigenetic reprogramming and infertility, and are the starting point for attempts to make oogonia and prospermatogonia in culture.
cell_types.maturation_note: hPGCLCs appear within 2-4 days of BMP exposure and correspond to early, pre-migratory PGCs; they stop expanding after about 5 days in the aggregates. Further maturation to oogonia-like cells needed about 4 months of aggregation culture with mouse fetal ovarian somatic cells (Yamashiro 2018 Science, PMID 30237246).

morphology.endpoint: Small floating aggregates in 96-well plates; hPGCLCs cannot be told apart by phase contrast and sit as one or a few clusters inside the aggregate, visible only with a reporter or after staining.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Flat compact colonies (primed cultures) or cultures kept in 4i medium on feeders.

stages.label: Competent precursor layer
stages.look: After activin A plus CHIR99021 the cells form a flatter, more spread monolayer with distinct cell borders (iMeLC / pre-mesendoderm).

stages.label: Fresh aggregates
stages.look: One small round aggregate per well of a low-binding 96-well plate.

stages.label: hPGCLC-containing aggregates
stages.look: Aggregates have grown and loosened; reporter-positive hPGCLCs form a cluster within them.

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Switched off in human PGCs and hPGCLCs (unlike mouse); a useful negative marker.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Moderately up in competent precursors; low in specified hPGCLCs.

markers.name: EOMES
markers.note: Primitive-streak gene that rises during the pre-induction step.

markers.name: SOX17
markers.note: Key specifier of human PGC fate; first germline factor detected.

markers.name: PRDM1
markers.note: Follows SOX17; represses somatic and endoderm genes. Used as a tdTomato reporter in the Sasaki system.

markers.name: TFAP2C
markers.note: Triple SOX17/PRDM1/TFAP2C positivity defines hPGCLCs; EGFP reporter in the Sasaki system.

markers.name: NANOS3
markers.note: Germline-specific; used as an mCherry or tdTomato knock-in reporter in the Surani-lab protocols.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Stays on in hPGCLCs, so it does not distinguish them from undifferentiated cells on its own.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Retained and increased in SOX17/PRDM1-positive cells.

markers.name: ALPL
markers.note: Sort with CD38 to isolate hPGCLCs without a reporter.

markers.name: CD38
markers.note: Absent on hESCs; about half of NANOS3-positive cells were CD38+ on day 4 and about 70% on day 5 in Irie 2015.

markers.name: ITGA6
markers.note: Used with EpCAM for reporter-free sorting in the Sasaki system.

markers.name: EPCAM
markers.note: Partner of ITGA6 for reporter-free sorting.

markers.name: FOXA2
markers.note: Endoderm marker; appears if SOX17 acts without enough PRDM1.

functional_assays: Flow cytometry for TNAP/CD38 or ITGA6/EpCAM double-positive cells
Onset of germline epigenetic reprogramming (fall in UHRF1 and DNMT3A, rise in TET1 and 5hmC)
Long-term maturation in aggregates with mouse fetal ovarian somatic cells (specialist assay)
qc: Cells co-express SOX17, PRDM1 and TFAP2C and have lost SOX2
A distinct TNAP+/CD38+ (or ITGA6+/EpCAM+) population is present by day 4 of aggregate culture

protocols.name: iMeLC route (activin A + CHIR, then BMP4 aggregates)
protocols.principle: Primed hiPSCs are first pushed for about two days into incipient mesoderm-like cells (iMeLCs) with activin A and a WNT agonist, which makes them competent; the cells are then aggregated in BMP4 with SCF, EGF and LIF to specify hPGCLCs.

source.authors: Sasaki K, Yokobayashi S, Nakamura T, et al.
source.title: Robust In Vitro Induction of Human Germ Cell Fate from Pluripotent Stem Cells

protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free primed hiPSCs passaged as single cells (the original work used laminin-511 E8 fragment and StemFit medium; not confirmed from the full text). Plates coated with fibronectin for the iMeLC step.

stages.name: iMeLC induction
stages.base_medium: GK15: GMEM + 15% KSR, 0.1 mM NEAA, 2 mM L-glutamine, 1 mM sodium pyruvate, penicillin-streptomycin, 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol

factors.name: Y-27632
factors.role: ROCK inhibitor; survival after single-cell plating

stages.feeding: No change reported; 44-48 h
actions: Plate single hiPSCs at 5 x 10^4 cells/cm^2 on fibronectin-coated wells in the induction medium
Culture for 44-48 h
stages.checkpoint: Flat, epithelial-looking sheet; do not extend beyond 48 h

stages.name: hPGCLC induction in aggregates
stages.base_medium: GK15: GMEM + 15% KSR, 0.1 mM NEAA, 2 mM L-glutamine, 1 mM sodium pyruvate, penicillin-streptomycin, 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol
stages.feeding: Medium not changed up to day 6 of induction
actions: Dissociate iMeLCs to single cells with TrypLE Select
Seed 5,000 cells per well in 100 µl in a low-cell-binding V-bottom 96-well plate
Analyse aggregates by flow cytometry between day 2 and day 6 of induction
stages.checkpoint: Reporter-positive or ITGA6+/EpCAM+ cells detectable from about day 2 of induction

tips: The length of the iMeLC step matters: competence is transient
Without a BLIMP1/TFAP2C reporter line, sort ITGA6+/EpCAM+ cells
A step-by-step version extending to oogonia is Yamashiro et al. 2020 Nat Protoc (PMID 32231324, DOI 10.1038/s41596-020-0297-5)
pitfalls: Induction efficiency varies widely between hiPSC lines and clones
LIF is given in units, not ng/ml; check the unit definition of your supplier
unverified: Sasaki 2015 full text was not accessible (cell.com blocks automated access). All concentrations, the 5 x 10^4 cells/cm^2 density, 44-48 h timing and 5,000 cells per well are taken from Kojima et al. 2021 Life Sci Alliance (PMID 33608411, PMC7918644), a paper from the same laboratory that states the induction was done as described previously
The original paper's cells per aggregate (may differ from 5,000), its reported efficiency, and the hiPSC maintenance conditions are not confirmed

protocols.name: 4i competent state, then BMP cytokine embryoids
protocols.principle: hESCs or hiPSCs held in '4i' medium (inhibitors of GSK3, MEK, p38 and JNK with LIF, bFGF and TGF-beta1) are reversibly competent for germ cell fate; a two-day pre-induction or direct aggregation in BMP2/BMP4 with LIF, SCF and EGF gives hPGCLCs.

source.authors: Irie N, Weinberger L, Tang WW, et al.
source.title: SOX17 is a critical specifier of human primordial germ cell fate

protocols.efficiency: About 27% NANOS3-mCherry/TNAP double-positive cells by day 4-5 after pre-induction; about 46% when induced directly from 4i cells; about 31% TNAP/CD38 double-positive from a 4i hiPSC line; about 0-5% from conventional bFGF cultures
protocols.start_requirements: Cells kept for more than 2 weeks in 4i medium on irradiated MEFs: knockout DMEM, 20% KSR, 2 mM L-glutamine, 0.1 mM NEAA, 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol, 20 ng/ml human LIF, 8 ng/ml bFGF, 1 ng/ml TGF-beta1, 3 µM CHIR99021, 1 µM PD0325901, 5 µM SB203580, 5 µM SP600125. Passage every 3-5 days with TrypLE Express; 10 µM Y-27632 for 24 h after passage.

stages.name: Pre-induction

factors.name: bFGF
factors.role: Primes towards a post-implantation epiblast-like state

factors.name: TGF-beta1 or activin A
factors.conc: 1 ng/ml TGF-beta1 or 20 ng/ml activin A

stages.feeding: Change medium on day 1
actions: Dissociate 4i cells with TrypLE Express and pass through a 50 µm filter
Plate 4 x 10^5 cells per well of a 12-well plate coated with vitronectin/gelatin
stages.checkpoint: Cells attach and spread as a monolayer

stages.name: hPGCLC induction in embryoids
stages.base_medium: GMEM + 15% KSR, 0.1 mM NEAA, 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol, penicillin-streptomycin, 2 mM L-glutamine, 1 mM sodium pyruvate
stages.feeding: Not stated
actions: Dissociate with TrypLE and seed 2,000-4,000 cells per well in 200 µl in ultra-low attachment U-bottom 96-well plates
Analyse by flow cytometry on day 4-5 of embryoid culture
stages.checkpoint: Reporter intensity rises until day 4-5; hPGCLCs form one or a few clusters by day 4-8

materials: Human LIF, bFGF, TGF-beta1, activin A
tips: Cells can be induced directly from 4i culture without the pre-induction step, with a higher yield in the paper
TNAP plus CD38 allows sorting without a reporter
Competence is reversible: it is lost after more than 2 weeks back in conventional medium
pitfalls: hPGCLCs do not proliferate appreciably after about day 5
Long-term culture in kinase-inhibitor media can affect genome and epigenome stability; keep karyotype checks up to date (general caution, not from this paper)
unverified: Medium change schedule during the embryoid step is not stated
Day numbers here count pre-induction as days 0-2 and embryoid culture as days 2-7 (the paper counts embryoid days from 1)

protocols.name: 12 h pre-mesendoderm from conventional E8 cultures, then BMP embryoids
protocols.principle: Conventional primed hPSCs pass through a short window of germline competence about 12 h into mesendoderm induction with activin A and CHIR99021; aggregating the cells at that point in BMP with LIF, SCF and EGF gives hPGCLCs without any need for 4i culture.

source.authors: Kobayashi T, Zhang H, Tang WWC, et al.
source.title: Principles of early human development and germ cell program from conserved model systems

protocols.start_requirements: hPSCs on vitronectin in Essential 8, passaged every 3-5 days as clumps with 0.5 mM EDTA.

stages.name: Pre-mesendoderm (Pre-ME) induction
stages.base_medium: aRB27: Advanced RPMI 1640 + 1% B27, 0.1 mM NEAA, penicillin-streptomycin, 2 mM L-glutamine
stages.feeding: Single 12 h exposure
actions: Trypsinise to single cells
Seed 200,000 cells per well of a vitronectin-coated 12-well plate in induction medium
Harvest at 12 h; competence peaks at about 12 h and declines from about 18 h
stages.checkpoint: Moderate rise in primitive-streak genes (TBXT, MIXL1, EOMES) with only a slight fall in SOX2

stages.name: hPGCLC induction in embryoids
stages.feeding: Not stated
actions: Trypsinise Pre-ME cells and seed 4,000 cells per well in ultra-low attachment or PrimeSurface 96V plates
Analyse on day 4 of embryoid culture
stages.checkpoint: SOX17 appears by 12 h, TFAP2C by about 18 h; a cluster of SOX17/PRDM1/TFAP2C-positive cells sits in the middle of the embryoid by 48 h

tips: Timing of the pre-induction is the critical variable: 12 h gives germline competence, 24 h gives mesendoderm that makes endoderm or mesoderm instead
aRB27 as the embryoid base medium improved efficiency over GK15 for Pre-ME cells
BMP2 alone induces hPGCLCs but they do not survive extended culture without LIF, SCF and EGF
pitfalls: Letting pre-induction run past about 18 h sharply lowers yield
unverified: No single efficiency figure was extracted from the text (values are in figures)
Medium change schedule during embryoid culture is not stated
Note the LIF dose here (10 ng/ml) differs from Irie 2015 (1 µg/ml) as printed in the two papers

cell_types.notes: hPGCLCs are an early germ cell state, not gametes. Efficiency is strongly line- and clone-dependent, and reporter lines or surface-marker sorting are needed to purify the cells. The three protocols differ mainly in how germline competence is obtained (iMeLC, 4i or a 12 h pre-mesendoderm step); BMP is the common inducer. Check local rules on human germline research before starting.

cell_types.name: Trophoblast (stem cells, syncytio- and extravillous trophoblast)
cell_types.summary: Trophoblasts are the epithelial cells of the placenta: self-renewing cytotrophoblast gives rise to hormone-secreting syncytiotrophoblast and invasive extravillous trophoblast. PSC-derived trophoblast is used to model implantation, placental disorders such as pre-eclampsia, and infection at the maternal-fetal interface without needing placental tissue.
cell_types.maturation_note: BMP4-based conversion of primed cells gives KRT7+ epithelium within 2 days and hormone secretion from about day 5; naive-derived trophectoderm takes 3 days, while stable trophoblast stem cell lines need 5-10 passages. Terminal differentiation adds 6 days (syncytiotrophoblast) or 8 days (extravillous trophoblast).

morphology.endpoint: Trophoblast stem cells grow as tight cobblestone epithelial colonies; syncytiotrophoblast forms large multinucleated patches (or floating cyst-like spheres in 3D); extravillous trophoblast cells are elongated and spindle-shaped.

stages.label: Naive or primed colonies
stages.look: Dome-shaped naive colonies on feeders, or flat primed colonies, depending on the protocol.

stages.label: Flattened trophectoderm-like sheet
stages.look: Cells become polygonal and flat; BMP4-treated primed colonies turn into a KRT7+ epithelium within about 2 days.

stages.label: Trophoblast stem cell colonies
stages.look: Homogeneous cobblestone colonies with bright borders once proliferative hTSCs take over (passage 5-10).

stages.label: Syncytiotrophoblast
stages.look: Fused, multinucleated areas without visible cell borders; in 3D culture, floating syncytial spheres retained on a 40 µm strainer.

stages.label: Extravillous trophoblast
stages.look: Elongated, spindle-shaped, loosely attached cells in Matrigel-containing medium.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be lost.

markers.name: KLF17
markers.note: Naive-state marker; confirms the starting cells and should fall in hTSCs.

markers.name: CDX2
markers.note: Transient: most BAP-treated cells are positive at 24-48 h, then it declines.

markers.name: TACSTD2
markers.note: With ENPEP, identifies naive-derived trophectoderm on day 3 (50-60% double-positive reported).

markers.name: ENPEP
markers.note: Sort TACSTD2+ENPEP+ cells before moving to ACE medium.

markers.name: GATA3
markers.note: Pan-trophoblast transcription factor; also expressed in amnion, so not sufficient alone.

markers.name: KRT7
markers.note: Pan-trophoblast marker; nearly all BAP-treated cells positive by 48 h.

markers.name: TFAP2C
markers.note: Trophoblast transcription factor.

markers.name: TP63
markers.note: Cytotrophoblast / stem-cell marker.

markers.name: TEAD4
markers.note: Stem-cell marker; falls on syncytiotrophoblast differentiation.

markers.name: ELF5
markers.note: About 15-fold or more above naive hPSCs in good hTSCs per the Dong & Theunissen protocol.

markers.name: ITGA6
markers.note: ITGA6/EGFR double-positive fraction is the standard hTSC purity readout.

markers.name: CGB3
markers.note: Syncytiotrophoblast hormone; measure hCG in the medium.

markers.name: HLA-G
markers.note: Extravillous trophoblast marker; at least 80% positive expected at day 8 of EVT differentiation.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Mesoderm; appears if FGF/activin signalling is not suppressed during BMP4 treatment.

functional_assays: hCG (and progesterone, PGF) secretion by ELISA
Cell fusion / multinucleation count
Matrigel invasion assay for extravillous trophoblast
Flow cytometry for ITGA6/EGFR (stem cells) and HLA-G (EVT)
qc: At least 80% ITGA6+/EGFR+ cells in naive-derived hTSCs, reaching about 95% at passage 10 or later
At least 80% HLA-G+ cells at day 8 of EVT differentiation
CGB and SDC1 clearly up in syncytiotrophoblast relative to hTSCs

protocols.name: BAP: BMP4 with activin and FGF inhibitors (primed cells)
protocols.principle: Primed hESCs given BMP4 while FGF2 is withdrawn and activin/nodal and FGF signalling are blocked (A83-01 and PD173074) convert quickly and uniformly to a KRT7+ trophoblast-like epithelium that later makes HLA-G+ and hormone-secreting syncytial cells.

source.authors: Amita M, Adachi K, Alexenko AP, et al.
source.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
source.title: Complete and unidirectional conversion of human embryonic stem cells to trophoblast by BMP4

protocols.efficiency: More than 40% KRT7+ within 24 h and almost all cells KRT7+ by 48 h with BAP (about 95% by day 4 with BMP4 alone)
protocols.start_requirements: Primed hESCs (H1, H9) on Matrigel in mTeSR1. Passage as clumps with dispase (1 mg/ml, 3 min) at 1:12, about 1.2 x 10^4 cells/cm^2.

stages.name: Conditioning in MEF-conditioned medium

factors.name: FGF2
factors.role: Keeps cells undifferentiated for one day in the new medium

stages.feeding: Single 24 h step
actions: The day after plating in mTeSR1, change to MEF-conditioned medium with FGF2
stages.checkpoint: Small undifferentiated colonies

stages.name: BAP treatment
stages.feeding: Change medium daily
actions: Withdraw FGF2 and add BMP4, A83-01 and PD173074
Collect spent medium daily if hormones are to be measured
End most experiments by day 9
stages.checkpoint: Nuclear CDX2 in most cells at day 2; hCG, progesterone and PGF in the medium from about day 5

tips: Colonies contain HLA-G+ cells by day 3-4 and syncytial areas by day 5-6
Conversion is slower in chemically defined media: about 70% KRT7+ at day 5 with BAP in the defined medium tested
pitfalls: Whether BMP4-treated primed cells are true trophoblast or partly amnion-like is still debated; confirm with several markers
Leaving FGF2 in, or omitting the inhibitors, allows mesoderm (TBXT) to appear
The cells are a differentiating population, not a self-renewing stem cell line
unverified: Details were read through a summarising fetch of the PMC page (the structured full text was empty), not line by line
Day numbering is set here so that BAP addition is day 0; whether the paper's 'day 9' endpoint is counted from BAP addition or from plating was not confirmed

protocols.name: Naive hPSCs to trophoblast stem cells in Okae hTSC medium, then EVT or STB
protocols.principle: Naive hPSCs placed directly in the trophoblast stem cell medium of Okae et al. (EGF, CHIR99021, TGF-beta inhibitors, valproic acid, ROCK inhibitor) convert over several passages into self-renewing hTSCs; primed cells do not. The hTSCs are then differentiated with the Okae conditions to extravillous trophoblast (NRG1, A83-01, Matrigel) or syncytiotrophoblast (forskolin).

source.authors: Dong C, Beltcheva M, Gontarz P, et al.
source.title: Derivation of trophoblast stem cells from naïve human pluripotent stem cells

protocols.efficiency: Highly proliferative hTSCs emerge between passage 5 and 10; good cultures are at least 80% ITGA6+/EGFR+ (about 95% from passage 10)
protocols.start_requirements: A confluent well of naive hPSCs in 5i/L/A or PXGL medium on MEF feeders (5% O2). Plates coated with 5 µg/ml collagen IV (at least 3 h or overnight at 37 °C).

stages.name: hTSC derivation and expansion
stages.base_medium: DMEM/F12 + 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol, 0.2% FBS, 0.5% penicillin-streptomycin, 0.3% BSA, 1% ITS-X
stages.feeding: Change medium every 2 days
actions: Dissociate naive cells to single cells with TrypLE Express (5 min)
Seed 0.5-1.0 x 10^6 cells per collagen IV-coated well of a 6-well plate in 2 ml hTSC medium; 5% CO2, 20% O2
Passage 1:2 at 80-100% confluence; cells grow slowly for the first few passages
Once homogeneous (5-10 passages), passage every 3 days at 1:4
stages.checkpoint: At least 80% ITGA6+/EGFR+ by flow; ELF5, KRT7 and GATA3 strongly up versus naive cells

stages.name: EVT differentiation, days 0-3
stages.base_medium: DMEM/F12 + 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol, 0.5% penicillin-streptomycin, 0.3% BSA, 1% ITS-X + 4% KSR

factors.name: Matrigel
factors.role: Matrix signal; add just after resuspending the cells

stages.feeding: Single dose
actions: Seed 0.75 x 10^5 hTSCs per well of a 6-well plate coated with 1 µg/ml collagen IV in 2 ml medium

stages.name: EVT differentiation, days 3-6
stages.base_medium: DMEM/F12 + 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol, 0.5% penicillin-streptomycin, 0.3% BSA, 1% ITS-X + 4% KSR
stages.feeding: Single change on day 3
actions: Replace medium; NRG1 is omitted from day 3

stages.name: EVT differentiation, days 6-8
stages.feeding: Single change on day 6
actions: Replace medium without KSR
Analyse on day 8 of differentiation
stages.checkpoint: At least 80% HLA-G+; HLA-G and MMP2 mRNA strongly up versus hTSCs

tips: Syncytiotrophoblast alternative from the same hTSCs: 2.5 x 10^5 cells per well of an ultra-low attachment 6-well plate in 3 ml 3D STB medium (DMEM/F12 + 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol, 0.5% penicillin-streptomycin, 0.3% BSA, 1% ITS-X, 50 ng/ml EGF, 2.5 µM Y-27632, 2 µM forskolin, 4% KSR); add another 3 ml on day 3 and collect on a 40 µm strainer on day 6. A 2D version uses 1 x 10^5 cells per well on 2.5 µg/ml collagen IV in the same medium without EGF

The hTSC medium and the EVT/STB conditions are those of Okae et al. 2018 (Cell Stem Cell 22:50-63, PMID 29249463, DOI 10.1016/j.stem.2017.11.004), who derived hTSCs from blastocysts and first-trimester placenta
A step-by-step version is Dong & Theunissen 2022 Methods Mol Biol (PMID 34870832, DOI 10.1007/978-1-0716-1908-7_7)
pitfalls: Primed hPSCs do not give hTSCs in this medium; a well-characterised naive culture is the prerequisite
Expect a slow, heterogeneous phase for the first passages; do not discard early
Day numbers after derivation are nominal: differentiation starts whenever a stable hTSC line is in hand
unverified: The 30-day derivation length is an approximation of '5-10 passages' and is not a figure from the paper

protocols.name: Naive hPSCs to trophectoderm in 3 days, then cytotrophoblast in ACE medium

source.title: Optimized protocol for naive human pluripotent stem cell-derived trophoblast induction

factors.role: ROCK inhibitor for the first 24 h

stages.name: Cytotrophoblast (nCT) in ACE medium

cell_types.name: Amnion-like cells
cell_types.summary: The amnion is the thin squamous epithelium that splits from the epiblast at implantation and encloses the embryo in the amniotic cavity. hPSC-derived amnion-like cells are used to model peri-implantation human development, in particular amniogenesis and the signals the amnion sends to the epiblast.
cell_types.maturation_note: Squamous amnion-like tissue appears 2-4 days after the 3D matrix overlay or within 48 h of BMP4; it corresponds to nascent amnion and is the end point of these cultures.

stages.label: Single cells on matrix
stages.look: Dissociated hPSCs seeded at 30,000 cells/cm^2 on a soft gel bed or on a membrane.

stages.label: Columnar epiblast-like cysts

stages.label: Squamous amnion-like cysts

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Lost as cysts turn squamous (days 2-4).

markers.name: POU5F1

markers.name: SOX2

markers.name: CDH1

markers.name: EZR

markers.name: TFAP2A

markers.name: GATA3
markers.note: Up in amnion-like cells but shared with trophoblast.

markers.name: CDX2

markers.name: SOX17

stages.name: Seeding on the gel bed

factors.name: Y-27632
factors.role: ROCK inhibitor; survival of single cells

Plate at 30,000 cells/cm^2 on the gel bed in mTeSR1 with Y-27632

stages.name: 3D overlay and amniogenesis

factors.role: Dilute matrix overlay that supplies the 3D cue

Analyse on day 5

protocols.name: BMP4 on Transwell membranes (Transwell-AMLC)

source.title: Controlled modelling of human epiblast and amnion development using stem cells

stages.name: Seeding on the membrane

actions: Seed dissociated hPSCs onto the coated insert (density printed as 30 x 10^n cells/cm^2; see unverified)
stages.checkpoint: Attached, even layer

stages.name: BMP4 induction

cell_types.name: Gastruloids / 2D micropattern gastrulation models
cell_types.summary: Gastruloids are hPSC colonies or aggregates that self-organise into ordered domains of the three germ layers, reproducing aspects of gastrulation that cannot be studied in human embryos. They are used to study signalling and patterning (BMP, WNT, Nodal), axis formation, and the effects of mutations or drugs on early development.
cell_types.maturation_note: Radial germ-layer rings are complete 42-48 h after BMP4 on micropatterns; 3D human gastruloids show anteroposterior organisation by 72 h. Neither model goes on to form organs.

stages.label: Confined pluripotent discs
stages.look: Circular colonies filling each adhesive island edge to edge a few hours after seeding.

stages.label: Ring formation
stages.look: Within 24 h of BMP4 a dense ring of cells forms at a reproducible radius, with flatter cells inside and outside.

stages.label: Patterned colony
stages.look: Dense SOX2+ centre, a multilayered primitive-streak-like ring, and large spread CDX2+ cells at the border.

stages.label: Elongated 3D gastruloid
stages.look: In the 3D version, aggregates become elongated with a distinct pole by 72 h.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Down-regulated in the centre as SOX2 rises.

markers.name: SOX2
markers.note: Central disc: prospective ectoderm.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Ring outside the SOX2 centre: primitive streak / mesoderm.

markers.name: EOMES

markers.name: SOX17

markers.note: Mesendoderm marker overlapping EOMES.

markers.name: CDX2
markers.note: Outer ring: trophoblast-like / extra-embryonic-like cells at the edge; also overlaps BRA in mesoderm.

markers.name: SMAD1
markers.note: BMP response becomes restricted to the colony edge by 24 h.

markers.name: CDH1
markers.note: Internalised in the streak-like ring as cells undergo EMT.

Perturbation with SB431542 (removes BRA and SOX17 domains) or siRNA against inhibitors

cell_types.name: Epiblast-like cells (EpiLC)
cell_types.summary: EpiLCs are the short-lived in vitro counterpart of the pre-gastrulation (E5.5-E6.5) mouse epiblast, made by pushing ground-state ESCs with activin A and bFGF for about two days. They are mainly used as the obligatory launch pad for primordial germ cell-like cells and for other post-implantation lineages, because this is the state in which cells are competent to respond to BMP4 with a germline fate.
cell_types.maturation_note: Competence is transient: it peaks around 44-48 h of induction and is lost by about day 3, so EpiLCs are used immediately rather than expanded.

morphology.endpoint: A flat, sub-confluent sheet of small, tightly packed cells with much less three-dimensional doming than naive ESC colonies. Colony borders blur as the sheet spreads, and the culture looks uniform rather than patchy.

stages.label: Flattening on fibronectin

stages.label: Sub-confluent epiblast-like sheet
stages.look: An even, sub-confluent monolayer of small uniform cells; this is the point at which germline competence is highest.

factors.name: bFGF

cell_types.name: Primordial germ cell-like cells
cell_types.summary: PGCLCs are the in vitro counterpart of nascent mouse primordial germ cells, induced from epiblast-like cells with a high dose of BMP4 in floating aggregates. They are the entry point to in vitro gametogenesis: transplanted into germ-cell-less testes they give fertile sperm, and aggregated with embryonic gonadal somatic cells they go on to make oocytes.
cell_types.maturation_note: Freshly induced cells correspond roughly to E9.5 migratory germ cells and arrest there; going further needs expansion culture on steel-factor feeders or reaggregation with embryonic gonadal somatic cells.

morphology.endpoint: Compact, smooth floating aggregates a few hundred micrometres across, with the germline cells sitting as a bright cluster that is obvious only with a reporter or after staining; the rest of the aggregate is somatic.

stages.label: Naive ESC colonies
stages.look: Round, domed, tightly packed colonies in 2i+LIF.

stages.label: Epiblast-like monolayer
stages.look: Flat, even, sub-confluent sheet on fibronectin at the competence window.

stages.label: Early floating aggregates
stages.look: Cells coalesce at the bottom of the U-bottom well into a single loose ball within the first day.

stages.label: Germline-containing aggregates
stages.look: Smooth, compact spheres; under fluorescence a discrete reporter-bright cluster marks the germline population.

stages.label: Expanded germ cells on feeders
stages.look: Small, round, refractile cells growing in loose clumps on a flat feeder layer.

markers.name: Prdm1
markers.note: The founding germline determinant; the Blimp1-mVenus reporter is the standard live readout.

markers.name: Dppa3
markers.note: Second-wave germline marker; the Stella-ECFP reporter comes up after Blimp1-mVenus.

markers.name: Prdm14
markers.note: Germline factor; on its own it suffices to push epiblast-like cells to a germline state.

markers.name: Tfap2c
markers.note: Third member of the germline transcription factor trio.

markers.name: Nanos3
markers.note: Germ-cell-specific gene, upregulated in induced germline cells.

markers.name: Dnd1
markers.note: Germ-cell RNA-binding protein, upregulated.

markers.name: Nanog
markers.note: Unusually, pluripotency genes come back up in germline cells rather than switching off.

markers.name: Sox2
markers.note: Also re-expressed in the germline population.

markers.name: Itgb3
markers.note: With SSEA1, lets germline cells be sorted without a reporter and away from tumorigenic undifferentiated cells.

markers.name: Fut4
markers.note: Surface marker used together with integrin-beta3 for sorting.

markers.name: Dnmt3b
markers.note: De novo methyltransferase, downregulated as the germline epigenome is reset.

markers.name: Uhrf1
markers.note: Also downregulated, part of the methylation-maintenance shutdown.

markers.name: Hoxb1
markers.note: Somatic Hox gene; stays low in germline cells, unlike neighbouring somatic cells in the aggregate. (Marks: Somatic mesoderm.)

markers.name: Ddx4
markers.note: Comes on only after the cells reach a gonadal environment, not in freshly induced aggregates. (Marks: Gonadal germ cell.)

Reaggregation with embryonic gonadal somatic cells (reconstituted testis or ovary)
Genome-wide DNA methylation measurement during expansion
Embryonic germ cell colony-forming assay

Expansion culture should give more than an 8-fold increase in cell number (Ishikura 2022); Ohta 2017 reports ~20-fold on average and up to ~50-fold
Sorted population free of reporter-negative cells, which otherwise carry tumorigenic undifferentiated cells into transplants

protocols.name: Cytokine-induced PGCLCs from EpiLC aggregates (BMP4 + LIF + SCF + EGF)

stages.name: EpiLC induction

factors.name: KnockOut Serum Replacement

stages.feeding: Medium changed once at 24 h
actions: Plate ESCs on fibronectin in EpiLC induction medium
Harvest at ~44-48 h, at the peak of germline competence

stages.name: Floating aggregation with BMP4

factors.name: BMP4

factors.name: BMP8a

factors.name: SCF

Dissociation that leaves clumps, giving uneven aggregates.
Carrying undifferentiated cells into transplantation experiments if sorting is skipped.

The exact cells-per-aggregate number used in the original paper is not confirmed (restating papers give 1,000-2,000).
The induction efficiency (percent reporter-positive cells) reported in the original paper could not be read.
Whether the original used Lipidure-coated or other low-binding plates is not confirmed.

protocols.principle: A tightened version of the cytokine route: a fixed number of EpiLCs is aggregated in BMP4-containing medium, and the aggregates are harvested at about 90 h, when the germline reporter is bright but the second reporter has only just begun - the window in which the cells still expand on feeders.

protocols.principle: Sorted day-4 germline cells are expanded on steel-factor-presenting feeders with two drugs that raise cAMP by different routes; during this expansion the cells erase their DNA methylome, reproducing the epigenetic reset of gonadal germ cells.

source.authors: Ohta H, Kurimoto K, Okamoto I, Nakamura T, Yabuta Y, Miyauchi H, et al.
source.title: In vitro expansion of mouse primordial germ cell-like cells recapitulates an epigenetic blank slate

stages.name: Expansion on steel-factor feeders
stages.base_medium: GMEM with 10% KSR, 2.5% FCS, 0.1 mM NEAA, 1 mM sodium pyruvate, 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol, 2 mM L-glutamine, antibiotics

cell_types.notes: Almost every failure traces back to the epiblast-like step: the competence window is narrow, KSR must stay at 1%, and the right harvest time has to be found per line. cell_types.name: Gastruloids
cell_types.summary: Gastruloids are small aggregates of mouse ESCs that break symmetry, specify the three germ layers and elongate along an anteroposterior axis, reproducing post-occipital embryonic patterning including collinear Hox expression. They are used as an accessible stand-in for the post-implantation embryo, for axis formation, somitogenesis and signalling studies that would be impractical with embryos.
cell_types.maturation_note: Elongation is clearest at 114-120 h; past 120 h in a 96-well plate the structures adhere and lose organisation, so extended culture to 168 h is done in larger volumes on an orbital shaker.

morphology.endpoint: An elongated, roughly tadpole-shaped structure a few hundred micrometres long: one end bright and smooth under phase contrast (the elongating posterior), the other rounded and darker with a loose coat of shed cells (anterior). Internal epithelial structures become visible in extended culture.

stages.label: Single cells in a droplet
stages.look: Dispersed single cells sitting in a 40 ul droplet at the bottom of a U-bottom well.

stages.label: Coalescing aggregate
stages.look: Cells have fallen together into a ragged ball in which individual cells are already hard to tell apart.

stages.label: Clean spheroid
stages.look: A smooth, free-floating sphere about 150-200 um across; the well floor is mostly clean.

stages.label: Ovoid after the Wnt pulse
stages.look: Grown further, with local narrowing giving an ovoid outline and a thin rough coating of extruded cells.

stages.label: Elongating axis
stages.look: A clear long axis appears, bright and smooth at one end, round and dark at the other.

stages.label: Elongated gastruloid
stages.look: A long extension projecting from the darker rounded anterior mass; at least 70% of a good plate is elongating by this point.

markers.name: T
markers.note: The defining readout: it localises to one end, which is what defines the posterior pole. (Marks: Posterior / primitive streak.)

markers.name: Sox2
markers.note: Expressed in a domain extending away from the T-positive tip; marks tubular neural epithelia in late aggregates. (Marks: Neural / neuromesodermal.)

markers.name: Sox1
markers.note: Neural progenitor marker, reported with a Sox1::GFP reporter; anterior Sox1 with posterior T is the patterning criterion.

markers.name: Cdx2
markers.note: Posterior marker that extends away from the T-expressing tip, giving a dorsoventral-like organisation. (Marks: Posterior / caudal epiblast.)

markers.name: Sox17
markers.note: Marks endodermal pockets, typically in the anterior part of the structure.

markers.name: Foxa2
markers.note: Used alongside Sox17 to confirm endodermal identity. (Marks: Endoderm / axial mesendoderm.)

markers.name: Otx2
markers.note: Found in anterior epithelia and neural rosettes; central to the anterior neural phenotype of Wnt-inhibited aggregates.

markers.name: Tbx6
markers.note: Paraxial mesoderm marker; a TBX6::EYFP reporter line was used to score responses to signals.

markers.name: Cdh1
markers.note: Used to follow epithelial organisation within the aggregate. (Marks: Epithelium.)

markers.name: Nodal
markers.note: Timed interaction between Nodal and Wnt is what localises T expression to one end.

markers.name: Pou5f1
markers.note: Starting state marker; should fall away as germ-layer markers come up. (Marks: Pluripotent.)

markers.name: Hoxb1
markers.note: Hox genes come on collinearly along the extending axis, the hallmark of post-occipital identity. (Marks: Axial elongation.)

markers.name: Mixl1
markers.note: Should be off in the starting epiblast-like aggregate; useful as a negative control before patterning. (Marks: Mesendoderm.)

At least 70% of gastruloids elongating by 114 h under optimal conditions (Girgin 2018 Protocol Exchange)

Wash the cells twice in PBS to remove carried-over serum

Pipette 40 ul per well into a non-treated U-bottom 96-well plate

stages.name: Wnt pulse

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.conc: 3 uM (added as 150 ul of a 3 uM solution; effective concentration in the well ~2.37 uM after dilution)
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; switches Wnt on for 24 h

Pipette firmly enough to dislodge any aggregate starting to stick
Incubate 24 h

Coating the plate with gelatin or fibronectin, which must not be done.

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; a single 24 h pulse

stages.feeding: 150 ul of secondary medium added per well
actions: Prepare 3 uM CHIR99021 in N2B27 (16 ml is ample for one plate)
Add 150 ul per well
Incubate 24 h
stages.checkpoint: At 72 h aggregates have grown, some show local narrowing and an ovoid shape, with a thin rough coat of shed cells

stages.name: Daily washout
stages.feeding: 150 ul exchanged at 72, 96 and 120 h
actions: Remove 150 ul from the side of each well with the pipette at an angle
Add 150 ul fresh pre-warmed N2B27 with enough force to move the gastruloid
stages.checkpoint: At 96 h many aggregates have a clear long axis: one end bright and smooth (posterior, elongating), the other round and dark with loose cells (anterior)

stages.name: Extended shaking culture
stages.feeding: 700 ul per well; 400 ul exchanged at 144 h
actions: At 120 h transfer gastruloids individually into low-attachment 24-well plates in 700 ul N2B27, using a P1000 tip cut about 5 mm from the end
Incubate on an incubator-compatible orbital shaker at 40 rpm for 48 h
Exchange 400 ul of medium at 144 h
stages.checkpoint: By 168 h the elongation is long and thin, internal epithelial structures are visible by phase contrast, and the anterior end may be broad

tips: Optimum viewing time for the elongation is about 114-120 h.
Cells grown in 2i conditions also work, but elongation is slightly delayed relative to serum/LIF cells.
iPSC lines generally need more starting cells (600-800 per well) than ESC lines (300).
pitfalls: Many small satellite aggregates per well mean the cell density was underestimated when counting.
Evaporation from the 40 ul droplets during the first 48 h, worst in peripheral wells.
Aggregates adhering after 120 h unless moved to the shaking extended culture.
N2B27 batch variation, which shows up as aggregates decompacting from the edge inwards.
unverified: This is a Protocol Exchange article; its DOI (10.1038/protex.2018.094) comes from the Cambridge repository record for the accepted manuscript, not from a PubMed entry, and it has no PMID. Numbers were read from the accepted manuscript PDF.
Marker and patterning claims are in the associated Nature paper (Beccari 2018), not in this protocol.

protocols.name: Gastruloids from epiblast-like aggregates with Wnt inhibition (anterior neural)
protocols.principle: Starting from epiblast-like aggregates formed in microwells rather than from naive ESCs, and inhibiting rather than activating Wnt early on, gives structures that elongate without any exogenous Wnt pulse and go on to form anterior neural tissue that standard gastruloids lack.

source.authors: Girgin MU, Broguiere N, Mattolini L, Lutolf MP
source.title: Gastruloids generated without exogenous Wnt activation develop anterior neural tissues

protocols.efficiency: About 50% of aggregates show posterior T/BRA with anterior SOX1 at 144 h with the Wnt inhibitor, against about 10% without it; classical gastruloids never showed SOX1 anterior to T/BRA in this comparison
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ESCs in s2iL (DMEM+GlutaMAX, 10% ESC-qualified FBS, pyruvate, NEAA, 2-mercaptoethanol, pen/strep, 3 uM CHIR99021, 1 uM PD0325901, LIF), seeded at 50,000-60,000 cells per 6-well and cultured 2-3 days; dissociate with Accutase and wash twice in PBS.

stages.name: Epiblast-like aggregate formation
stages.base_medium: N2B27 (DMEM/F12 + Neurobasal, 0.5x N2, 0.5x B27, 0.5x GlutaMAX, pyruvate, NEAA, 2-mercaptoethanol)

factors.name: XAV939
factors.role: Tankyrase inhibitor; blocks Wnt and is what allows anterior neural tissue later

stages.feeding: 35 ul of cell suspension onto the array, then 1 ml medium; no change for 72 h
actions: Equilibrate 400 um PEG microwell arrays with 50 ul medium for 30 min at 37 C
Seed 35 ul of a 484,000 cells/ml suspension to give 100-150 cells per microwell
Let cells sediment for 20-30 min, then add 1 ml medium gently from the side
Culture at least 72 h
stages.checkpoint: Smooth aggregates, for 100 cells/well no more than about 220 um in diameter

stages.name: Transfer to 96-well plates
stages.feeding: 180 ul N2B27 per well with the aggregate added in 10 ul
actions: At about 72-80 h flush the aggregates off the array with N2B27 into a non-treated 10 cm dish
Pick single, undamaged, size-matched aggregates in 10 ul under a stereomicroscope
Transfer each into a well of an ultra-low-attachment U-bottom 96-well plate containing 180 ul N2B27
stages.checkpoint: One intact aggregate with smooth edges per well

stages.name: Elongation without exogenous Wnt
stages.feeding: 150 ul exchanged every 24 h until 168 h
actions: Change 150 ul of medium every 24 h with a multichannel pipette
Score morphology and reporter expression at 144 and 168 h
stages.checkpoint: Axial elongation with posterior T/BRA at the tip and anterior SOX1, plus SOX17-positive anterior endodermal pockets and OTX2-positive neural rosettes

materials: PEG microwell arrays (400 um wells, 121 per array)
tips: Elongation and patterning depend strictly on the initial aggregate size: smaller aggregates do not hold the elongated shape.
A step-by-step bench version of this protocol is published separately (Girgin 2023, Bio-protocol), including the standard 300-cell gastruloid arm for comparison.
pitfalls: Shaking or swirling during seeding, which spoils the even distribution across microwells.
Damaging aggregates during the pick-and-transfer step.
Without the Wnt inhibitor, anteroposterior patterning is rare (~10%).

cell_types.notes: Starting cell number is the critical variable: around 300 (plus or minus 100) cells, roughly 100 um across, works; above about 600 cells the aggregates grow as disorganised embryoid bodies and below about 200 they fail to respond. iPSC lines generally need more cells than ESC lines. Timing of the Wnt pulse matters as much as the dose - the 48-72 h window gives maximum elongation, while pulses applied earlier or later give variable or multi-polar responses, and the response is also cell-line dependent. Because a residual volume stays in the well during medium changes, the delivered CHIR99021 concentration is below nominal and carries over for a day or two.

cell_types.name: Optic cup / retinal organoids
cell_types.summary: Mouse ESC aggregates in serum-free floating culture with added extracellular matrix form a neuroepithelium that spontaneously generates retinal epithelium, evaginates optic vesicles and then invaginates into a two-walled optic cup, with neural retina inside and pigment epithelium outside. In extended culture the neural retina stratifies into the proper layers, which is why these organoids are the standard source of mouse photoreceptors for transplantation and retinal development work.
cell_types.maturation_note: Cup morphology appears by about day 9-10; stratified retina with photoreceptors needs several more weeks, usually at raised oxygen with retinoic acid and taurine added from around day 14.

morphology.endpoint: A floating aggregate carrying one or more cup-shaped structures: a bright, thick, laminated inner wall (neural retina) curving around a lumen, with a thinner outer wall that darkens with pigment as the culture goes on. A visible hinge marks the rim of each cup.

stages.label: Quick reaggregation
stages.look: Dissociated ESCs settling into the U-bottom well; aggregation begins within half an hour and is largely done within hours.

stages.label: Compact aggregate
stages.look: A smooth round aggregate whose surface starts to change once matrix has been added.

stages.label: Polarised neuroepithelium
stages.look: A hollow neuroepithelial shell with apical surface inward; faint retinal reporter patches begin to appear.

stages.label: Optic vesicles
stages.look: Thickened retinal patches bulge out from the aggregate surface as rounded vesicles, several per aggregate.

stages.label: Optic cups
stages.look: The distal part of each vesicle has folded inward, giving a double-walled cup with a bright laminated rim and a clear hinge.

stages.label: Stratified retina
stages.look: A thick, layered retinal wall with a dense outer photoreceptor zone; pigment is visible in the apposed epithelium in pigmented lines.

markers.name: Rax
markers.note: The earliest retinal readout; Rx::GFP reporter lines are the standard way to follow the induction. (Marks: Eyefield / retinal epithelium.)

markers.name: Pax6
markers.note: Confirms eye identity; important because Rax is also expressed in hypothalamic tissue. (Marks: Eyefield.)

markers.name: Lhx2
markers.note: Third eyefield transcription factor used to call eyefield induction.

markers.name: Vsx2
markers.note: Marks the inner wall of the cup, the neural retina.

markers.name: Mitf
markers.note: Marks the outer wall; its domain is induced by signals from the neighbouring non-retinal neuroepithelium. (Marks: Retinal pigment epithelium.)

markers.name: Otx2
markers.note: Co-expressed with Mitf in presumptive pigment epithelium, and later in photoreceptor precursors. (Marks: Pigment epithelium / photoreceptor.)

markers.name: Cdh2
markers.note: Apical (inner) side of the neuroepithelium; with laminin it shows the epithelium is correctly polarised.

markers.name: Crx
markers.note: Photoreceptor precursor marker; Crx-GFP lines are used to trace and sort them.

markers.name: Rcvrn
markers.note: Photoreceptor marker; detected in mouse ESC-derived retinal tissue from about day 24.

markers.name: Nrl
markers.note: Rod fate determinant; Nrl-GFP lines are used to follow rod production. (Marks: Rod photoreceptor.)

markers.name: Rho
markers.note: Mature rod marker; rhodopsin-promoter reporters label transplantable precursors.

markers.name: Sox2
markers.note: General neuroectoderm marker, used to place retinal regions within the wider neuroepithelium.

markers.name: Pou5f1
markers.note: Should disappear; persistence flags undifferentiated cells in the aggregate. (Marks: Pluripotent.)

markers.name: Six3
markers.note: Anterior neural and eyefield gene used in organoid gene-expression panels. (Marks: Anterior neural plate / eyefield.)

functional_assays: Live imaging of vesicle evagination and cup invagination
Scoring of laminated retinal structure on sections
Transplantation of sorted photoreceptor precursors into degenerate retina
Interkinetic nuclear migration of retinal progenitors
qc: Eyefield induction: 81% +/- 10% RAX+ organoids at day 7 with low seeding density (Volkner 2016)
Seeding density check: 1,500-3,000 cells/well gives 80% +/- 4% RAX+ organoids versus 10% +/- 4% at 6,000-9,000 cells/well (Volkner 2016)
Optic vesicles with a diameter above 300 um at days 5-7 and a flattened distal part by days 7-9 predict the best photoreceptor yield (Decembrini 2014)
Matrigel protein concentration checked per lot (9.1-10.1 mg/ml in Hiler 2016)

protocols.name: SFEBq optic cup: self-organising retinal epithelium in floating aggregates
protocols.principle: ESCs are quickly reaggregated in a low-adhesion U-bottom well in serum-free medium; with extracellular matrix added on day 1 the aggregate forms a neuroepithelium, patches of which turn on retinal identity, bulge out as vesicles and then invaginate on their own into a two-walled optic cup.

source.authors: Eiraku M, Takata N, Ishibashi H, Kawada M, Sakakura E, Okuda S, Sekiguchi K, Adachi T, Sasai Y
source.title: Self-organizing optic-cup morphogenesis in three-dimensional culture

protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ESCs (commonly an Rx::GFP reporter line) maintained feeder-free; dissociate to single cells, count with dead-cell exclusion, and plate immediately into low-adhesion wells.

stages.name: Quick reaggregation
stages.base_medium: GMEM with 1.5% KSR, 0.1 mM NEAA, 1 mM sodium pyruvate, 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol
stages.feeding: 3,000 cells per well in 100 ul; no feeding on day 0
actions: Dissociate ESCs to single cells and count accurately
Seed 3,000 cells per well of a low-adhesion U-bottom 96-well plate
Leave undisturbed; aggregation is essentially complete within a few hours
stages.checkpoint: A single compact aggregate per well by the end of day 0

stages.name: Matrix addition and neuroepithelium

factors.name: Growth-factor-reduced Matrigel
factors.role: Extracellular matrix; supports basement membrane formation and is required for efficient retinal differentiation

stages.feeding: Matrigel added directly to the well on day 1; no further change in this window
actions: Add growth-factor-reduced Matrigel on day 1 to a final 2% (v/v)
Culture undisturbed and watch the aggregate surface each day
stages.checkpoint: A polarised hollow neuroepithelium (N-cadherin inside, laminin outside) by about day 4, with the first faint retinal reporter patches at days 4-5

stages.name: Vesicle evagination and cup invagination
stages.base_medium: Same serum-free medium, then retinal maturation medium after the cups are isolated
stages.feeding: Aggregates kept floating; moved to maturation medium around days 7-9
actions: Watch for retinal epithelial patches evaginating into vesicles at days 6-7
Over the following two days the distal part of each vesicle invaginates on its own into a double-walled cup
Excise the retinal tissue and continue in retinal maturation medium for stratification
stages.checkpoint: Double-walled cups: an inner wall expressing neural retina markers (Vsx2/Chx10) and a rigid outer wall becoming pigment epithelium

tips: Each aggregate typically produces more than one retinal patch, so one well can yield several cups.
Pigment epithelium identity in the outer wall is induced by signals from the neighbouring non-retinal neuroepithelium, so do not trim the aggregate too aggressively.
Matrigel lot varies; later protocols from several labs stress routine lot testing.
pitfalls: Inaccurate cell counting: seeding density strongly determines whether eyefield tissue forms at all.
Matrigel omitted or at the wrong concentration, which kills retinal induction.
High ESC passage number or a poor starting state, after which retinal reporter expression simply does not appear.
unverified: The Nature 2011 and Nat Protoc 2012 full texts were not accessible in this session. Cell number (3,000 per well), 2% growth-factor-reduced Matrigel on day 1 and the GMEM/KSR base are taken from papers restating the SFEBq protocol: Takata 2016 (Data Brief, Eiraku lab), Gonzalez-Cordero 2013 (Nat Biotechnol, which states 1.5% KSR), Assawachananont 2014 (which describes raising KSR from 1.5% to 5% relative to the original) and Hiler 2016 (Nat Protoc).
Reported percentages of aggregates forming optic cups in the original paper were not verified.
Exact day of transfer to maturation medium and the oxygen tension used in the original are not confirmed; restating protocols vary (day 7-9, 40% O2).
The medium in Eiraku's own later work is a chemically defined medium rather than GMEM/KSR, so base-medium details differ between versions.

protocols.name: Whole-aggregate 3D retinal differentiation for photoreceptor production
protocols.principle: The same floating-aggregate route, but the retinal tissue is left inside the mother aggregate instead of being dissected out, and the culture is carried on for weeks in a simple maturation medium with retinoic acid and taurine so that transplantable photoreceptor precursors accumulate.

source.authors: Gonzalez-Cordero A, West EL, Pearson RA, Duran Y, Carvalho LS, Chu CJ, et al.
source.title: Photoreceptor precursors derived from three-dimensional embryonic stem cell cultures integrate and mature within adult degenerate retina

protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ESCs (EK.CCE, 129/SvEv) maintained as previously described, dissociated to single cells.

stages.name: Aggregation
stages.base_medium: GMEM with 1.5% KSR, 0.1 mM NEAA, 1 mM sodium pyruvate, 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol
stages.feeding: 3 x 10^4 cells per ml of differentiation medium, plated into low-binding 96-well plates
actions: Resuspend dissociated ESCs at 3 x 10^4 cells per ml of differentiation medium
Plate into 96-well low-binding plates and incubate at 37 C, 5% CO2
stages.checkpoint: Embryoid-body-like aggregates formed within 24 h

stages.name: Matrix and early retinal morphogenesis

factors.name: Growth-factor-reduced Matrigel
factors.role: Extracellular matrix; added to each well on day 1

stages.feeding: Matrigel added day 1; aggregates otherwise left floating
actions: Add growth-factor-reduced Matrigel to each well on day 1 to a final 2%
Score morphology: continuous neuroepithelium, then thickened protruding optic-vesicle-like regions, then invaginated cups with a hinge region
stages.checkpoint: Optic-vesicle-like protrusions and, in a fraction of aggregates, invaginated cup structures with a visible hinge

stages.name: Long-term maturation
stages.base_medium: Retinal maturation medium (DMEM/F12 GlutaMAX with N2 supplement and penicillin/streptomycin)

factors.name: Taurine
factors.role: Added from day 14; supports photoreceptor differentiation

factors.name: Retinoic acid
factors.role: Added from day 14; drives photoreceptor maturation

stages.feeding: Medium changed every 2-3 days; aggregates replated more sparsely at day 27
actions: At day 9 transfer whole aggregates into retinal maturation medium in low-binding plates at 6 aggregates/cm2
Change medium every 2-3 days, adding taurine and retinoic acid from day 14
At day 27 transfer to fresh low-binding plates at 3 aggregates/cm2 with 50% medium changes
stages.checkpoint: Rhodopsin-promoter reporter expression marking photoreceptor precursors suitable for sorting or transplantation

tips: Keeping the retina inside the whole aggregate avoids the dissection step and still yields large numbers of photoreceptor precursors.
Replating at lower density late in the culture keeps the aggregates from fusing.
pitfalls: Aggregates fusing or crowding if plated too densely during maturation.
Scoring optic-cup formation inconsistently; this paper gives explicit morphological criteria (hinge region, protruding thickened neuroepithelium).
unverified: The fraction of aggregates forming optic cups is not stated as a single headline figure in the text read here.
Oxygen tension is not stated for this protocol.

protocols.name: Trisection protocol: higher retinal organoid yield without evagination
protocols.principle: Rather than selecting the minority of aggregates that evaginate an optic vesicle, the whole eyefield-stage neuroepithelium is cut into three at day 10, so that retinal tissue hidden in the main body of the aggregate is also harvested.

source.authors: Völkner M, Zschätzsch M, Rostovskaya M, Overall RW, Busskamp V, Anastassiadis K, Karl MO
source.title: Retinal Organoids from Pluripotent Stem Cells Efficiently Recapitulate Retinogenesis

protocols.efficiency: Starting aggregates form with 100% efficiency; eyefield induction occurs in 81% (81% +/- 10% RAX+ organoids at day 7), and trisection raises the yield of retinal organoids to 183%
protocols.start_requirements: E14TG2a wild-type or hPAX6-GFP transgenic mouse ESCs in ESC medium with 1,000 U/ml LIF and 1 uM PD0325901, passaged every 2-3 days with TrypLE Express.

stages.name: Aggregation and matrix
stages.feeding: Aggregates formed on day 0, Matrigel added day 1, cultured at 20% O2 to day 7
actions: Aggregate ESCs in 96-well plates (day 0)
Add 2% Matrigel on day 1
Culture at 20% oxygen until day 7
stages.checkpoint: By day 7, 81% of organoids are RAX-positive; eyefield regions self-pattern into presumptive pigment epithelium (MITF+ OTX2+) and neural retina (RAX+ VSX2+)

stages.name: Transfer to maturation medium
stages.feeding: Transferred to bacterial-grade Petri dishes
actions: Transfer organoids to bacterial-grade Petri dishes
Culture in retinal maturation medium 1 at 40% O2
stages.checkpoint: Organoids intact and enlarging, with retinal regions visible

stages.name: Trisection and retinogenesis

factors.name: EC23
factors.role: Retinoic acid receptor agonist, added day 10 to day 14

stages.feeding: Cultured in maturation medium 2 after trisection
actions: At day 10 trisect each organoid manually with fine surgical tweezers
Culture the pieces in retinal maturation medium 2
Add EC23 from day 10 to day 14
Follow stratification to day 21 and beyond
stages.checkpoint: Large stratified retinal organoids; timed Notch inhibition at this stage can bias them towards cone or rod photoreceptors

materials: ESC medium with LIF and PD0325901
tips: Seeding density decides eyefield efficiency: lower seeding (1,500-3,000 cells/well) gave 80% +/- 4% RAX+ organoids, while higher seeding (6,000-9,000 cells/well) gave only 10% +/- 4%.
Most eyefield tissue sits in the main body of the aggregate rather than in an evagination - only 35% +/- 10% of aggregates had RAX+ evaginations, so selecting evaginations throws most of it away.
Not every evagination is retinal: 31% +/- 7% were RAX-negative.
pitfalls: Seeding too many cells per well, which collapses eyefield induction.
Discarding the mother aggregate body, where most retinal tissue actually is.
This protocol does not reproduce optic-cup invagination morphology; it trades that for yield.
unverified: Exact cell number per well for the standard condition, the composition of the differentiation and maturation media and the Matrigel product details are in the supplementary experimental procedures, which were not read in this session.
Whether the day-0 medium matches the original SFEBq formulation is not confirmed here.

cell_types.notes: Two variables dominate: how many cells go into each well and which Matrigel lot is used. Different labs have pulled the protocol in different directions - raising KSR and adding a retinoic-acid-receptor antagonist for transplantable sheets (Assawachananont 2014), switching to N2/B27 with raised oxygen from the onset of photoreceptor differentiation (Decembrini 2014, which reports ~79% +/- 4.3% of aggregates with at least one retinal structure for its best clone), or cutting the whole eyefield neuroepithelium into three to triple the yield at the cost of cup morphology (Volkner 2016). Decide first whether you want the cup shape or the photoreceptor numbers, because the protocols diverge on exactly that point.

cell_types.name: Neural progenitors and neurons (N2B27 monolayer)
cell_types.summary: Sox1+ neuroepithelial progenitors and the neurons they produce, made from mouse ES cells either as an adherent monolayer in serum-free N2B27 or through retinoic-acid-treated aggregates. They are used to study exit from pluripotency and neural commitment, to derive neural stem cell lines, and as a source of defined glutamatergic or cortical neurons.
cell_types.maturation_note: Sox1+ progenitors by day 4-6 and the first Tubb3+ neurons around day 6 in monolayer; aggregate and cortical protocols give plated neurons from day 8-14, with synaptic activity about 10 days after plating.

morphology.endpoint: A carpet of small neural progenitors, often arranged in rosette-like rings, with phase-bright neuronal cell bodies on top sending out long thin neurites that join into a network. Flat glial cells appear underneath in older cultures.

stages.label: ES cells at plating
stages.look: Single cells and small tight clumps at low density shortly after replating from compact, sharp-edged ES colonies.

stages.label: Flattening monolayer
stages.look: Cells spread out and lose the domed colony shape; some floating dead cells are normal in the first days.

stages.label: Neural progenitors
stages.look: Dense fields of small elongated Sox1+ cells that pack into ridges and rosette-like rings as the dish fills.

stages.label: First neurons
stages.look: Small phase-bright cell bodies with fine processes appear on top of the progenitor layer.

stages.label: Neuronal network
stages.look: After replating on laminin, well-separated neurons with long branching neurites form a network.

markers.name: Pou5f1
markers.note: Should disappear as Sox1 comes on; by day 3 a cell is either Oct4+ or Sox1+, not both (Mulas 2019). Persisting Oct4+ clusters mean density was too high or feeding was skipped.

markers.name: Nanog
markers.note: Lost early after LIF/2i withdrawal.

markers.name: Sox1
markers.note: Earliest specific neuroectoderm marker and the standard readout; 30-50% GFP+ on day 3 and 80-90% on day 4-5 in a good run (Mulas 2019).

markers.name: Sox2
markers.note: Also present in ES cells, so score Sox2+ Oct4- cells as committed progenitors (Lowell 2006).

markers.name: Nes
markers.note: Comes on roughly 12-24 h after the first Sox1-GFP+ cells; not exclusive to neural cells, so pair it with Sox1 or Sox2.

markers.name: Pax6
markers.note: Marks the radial-glia-like progenitors made by the aggregate + retinoic acid method and the dorsal forebrain progenitors of the cyclopamine method.

markers.name: Fabp7
markers.note: Radial glia marker scored alongside nestin and Pax6 in monolayer cultures (Lowell 2006).

markers.name: Foxg1
markers.note: Telencephalic identity; expected in the DDM/cyclopamine cortical protocol, not after retinoic acid.

markers.name: Tubb3
markers.note: First neurons appear around day 6 of monolayer differentiation.

markers.name: Map2
markers.note: Dendritic marker of maturing neurons.

markers.name: Slc17a7
markers.note: Glutamatergic identity; most neurons from the cyclopamine/DDM and aggregate/retinoic acid methods are glutamatergic.

markers.name: Slc17a6
markers.note: Second vesicular glutamate transporter used with VGLUT1 to score glutamatergic neurons.

markers.name: Slc32a1
markers.note: GABAergic neurons; a large VGAT+ fraction in a cortical run means ventral identity (cyclopamine missing or inactive).

markers.name: Gfap
markers.note: Astroglia follow neurons in time; many GFAP+ cells early usually means serum exposure.

Patch-clamp recording of action potentials and synaptic currents
Derivation of expandable NS cell lines in EGF + FGF-2
qc: Sox1-GFP+ 80-90% on day 4-5 from 2i-grown cells on laminin (Mulas 2019)
Little cell death on days 1-3; death on day 2-3 indicates a poor N2B27 batch (Mulas 2019)
No beating cells and no Oct4+ islands at day 5 (signs of too high a density or skipped medium changes)

protocols.name: N2B27 adherent monoculture on gelatin (Sox1-GFP 46C method)
protocols.principle: Mouse ES cells plated sparsely on gelatin in serum-free N2B27, with no LIF, serum or BMP, turn into Sox1+ neural progenitors on their own. Conversion depends on the FGF the cells make themselves, so density matters.

source.authors: Ying QL, Stavridis M, Griffiths D, Li M, Smith A.
source.title: Conversion of embryonic stem cells into neuroectodermal precursors in adherent monoculture.

protocols.efficiency: The abstract states that the bulk of ES cells convert to neural precursors, and that they can be purified by FACS or drug selection; the exact percentage was not read from the paper.
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free mouse ES cells, subconfluent and undifferentiated (for example GMEM + 10% serum + LIF on gelatin; the 46C Sox1-GFP line makes scoring easy). Cells must be dissociated and replated into N2B27, not just switched to it. Plate about 1 x 10^4 cells/cm2 (10,500 cells/cm2 = 1 x 10^5 cells per well of a 6-well plate) on 0.1% gelatin.

stages.name: Plating and neural commitment
stages.base_medium: N2B27: 1:1 mix of DMEM/F12 + modified N2 and Neurobasal + B27, with L-glutamine and 0.1 mM 2-mercaptoethanol

factors.name: No added growth factors
factors.role: Neural conversion relies on autocrine FGF; LIF, serum and BMP are left out

stages.feeding: Replace all medium with fresh N2B27 every 1-2 days
actions: Coat wells with 0.1% gelatin for at least 30 min
Dissociate ES cells to single cells with a gentle dissociation reagent, spin, resuspend in warm N2B27 and count
Plate at about 10,500 cells/cm2; do not swirl the plate, which piles cells in the centre
Change medium gently; flushing cells off changes the density and lowers efficiency
If survival after plating is poor, plate in a 1:3 mix of the N2 and B27 halves for the first two days
stages.checkpoint: Sox1-GFP (46C) becomes visible within 4-6 days; Oct4 is lost as Sox1 comes on

stages.name: Neurogenesis in the same medium

factors.name: No added growth factors
factors.role: Progenitors begin to leave the cell cycle and make neurons

stages.feeding: Fresh N2B27 every 1-2 days
actions: Keep feeding without replating if you only need a readout; replating at this stage costs viability
Fix and stain for beta-III-tubulin around day 6
stages.checkpoint: Sox1-GFP+ progenitors with beta-III-tubulin+ neurons among them by about day 6

materials: Modified N2 (insulin, apo-transferrin, progesterone, putrescine, sodium selenite, BSA)
tips: Titrate the plating density for every line and every batch of N2B27; 96-well plates needed roughly ten times the density per cm2 of 6-well plates in the JoVE write-up.
The Smith lab's later papers call 1 x 10^4 cells/cm2 the normal density for this method (Lowell 2006).
Another lab replated day 4 cells at 2 x 10^4 cells/cm2 on laminin with 5 ng/ml bFGF to carry cultures on to day 20 (Abranches 2009).
Progenitors from this method can be expanded as NS cell lines with EGF + FGF-2 (Conti 2005).
pitfalls: Too sparse and the cells die within 3 days; too dense (above roughly 36,500 cells/cm2 in 6-well plates) and far fewer cells turn on Sox1.
Some cell death in the first days is normal, but changing only the medium (without replating) always lowers efficiency.
Commercial N2 differs from the modified N2 used here; a poor N2B27 batch is the commonest cause of failure.
unverified: The full text of Ying 2003 (Nat Biotechnol) could not be opened; the plating density, coating, feeding schedule and timing given here come from the step-by-step JoVE protocol by Wongpaiboonwattana & Stavridis 2015 (PMID 26066640, doi 10.3791/52823; Stavridis is a co-author of Ying 2003), with the 1 x 10^4 cells/cm2 figure also stated in Lowell 2006 (PMID 16594731) and Abranches 2009 (PMID 19621087).
Ying 2003's own stated seeding density, medium-change interval and percentage of Sox1-GFP+ cells were not confirmed.
The JoVE recipe gives the final L-glutamine concentration as 0.2 mM as printed; not cross-checked against the original paper.
Stage 2 end day (7) is a convenient readout point, not a limit stated by the source.

protocols.name: N2B27 monolayer on laminin from 2i-cultured ES cells (Smith lab standard protocol)

cell_types.name: Spinal motor neurons
cell_types.summary: Cholinergic neurons of the ventral spinal cord that drive skeletal muscle, made from mouse ES cells in about a week by treating embryoid bodies with retinoic acid and a Hedgehog pathway agonist. cell_types.maturation_note: Hb9+ motor neurons are present in embryoid bodies from day 5-7; after dissociation they extend long neurites within 2 days, and electrical maturation continues over weeks in co-culture with muscle or glia.

morphology.endpoint: Floating embryoid bodies 150-200 µm across that glow with the Hb9-GFP reporter; once dissociated and plated on ornithine/laminin, phase-bright neuronal cell bodies, often in small clusters, send out long neurites.

stages.label: Patterned embryoid bodies

stages.label: Plated motor neurons

cell_types.notes: There are two families of method. The transgene-free monolayer route (Chal) needs careful control of Wnt and BMP signalling and gives mixed cultures of fibres, Pax7+ cells and non-muscle cells. The Pax3-induction route (Darabi/Perlingeiro) needs an engineered line and a cell sorter but gives a nearly pure, expandable progenitor population suited to transplantation. cell_types.name: Cardiomyocytes
cell_types.summary: Contracting heart muscle cells made from mouse ES or iPS cells, either as beating clusters in serum-grown embryoid bodies or as enriched monolayers after growth-factor-directed cardiac mesoderm induction. They are used to study early heart development, gene function in knockout lines, electrophysiology and drug effects on beating.
cell_types.maturation_note: First beating at about day 7-8; hanging-drop cultures are classed as early (about day 7-10), intermediate (about day 12-14) and late (about day 15-25) as the cells mature.

morphology.endpoint: Rhythmically contracting patches, strands or sheets. In plated embryoid bodies the beating areas sit within a mixed outgrowth of flat non-muscle cells; in the directed monolayer method larger synchronised sheets form.

stages.label: Undifferentiated ES colonies

stages.label: Embryoid bodies

stages.label: Plated cardiac mesoderm / EB outgrowth

stages.label: First beating areas
stages.look: Small clusters start to twitch, then contract rhythmically; in EB outgrowths they appear as discrete beating islands.

stages.label: Established contracting sheets

tips: This protocol is line-dependent by design: the paper's central finding is that each mouse (and human) line needs its own activin A/BMP4 optimum. Run a small activin × BMP4 matrix for every new line and BMP4/activin lot, reading out Flk-1/PdgfR-α at the end of the induction step.

Published doses for this same scheme differ between labs and lines: activin A 8 ng/ml + BMP4 0.5 ng/ml (E14-Tg2a; Cirino 2020), activin A 8 ng/ml + BMP4 1 ng/ml (Bardot 2017), and activin 6 ng/ml + BMP4 12.5 ng/ml as printed for A2Lox cells (Bouveret 2015). Later versions add a Wnt inhibitor at the plating step (XAV at 10 µM in Bardot 2017; IWR1 at 5 µM in Bouveret 2015) to push cardiac mesoderm towards cardiomyocytes.
Flk-1 and PdgfR-α co-expression is the in-process control; do not carry a batch forward if the double-positive population is small.

Growth-factor activity varies by lot, so re-titrate when a new lot arrives.
Timing is tight (48 h EBs, then about 40 h induction); delaying dissociation shifts the mesoderm that forms.
