protocols.name: Activin-induced c-Kit+/Cxcr4+ endoderm, then BMP4 + bFGF + activin A for hepatic fate (Gouon-Evans 2006)
protocols.principle: Activin A in serum-free re-aggregated EBs gives an endoderm progenitor population marked by Brachyury, Foxa2 and c-Kit (or c-Kit and Cxcr4). BMP4 together with bFGF and activin A then specifies these progenitors to a hepatic fate, and plated cells mature into Afp/albumin-positive hepatocyte-like cells.

source.authors: Gouon-Evans V, Boussemart L, Gadue P, et al.
source.title: BMP-4 is required for hepatic specification of mouse embryonic stem cell-derived definitive endoderm

protocols.efficiency: Hepatic populations 45-70% positive for Afp and albumin protein (abstract); a later review by the same lab lists about 55% Foxa2/c-Kit/Cxcr4+ endoderm after activin, then about 70% Afp+ and 60% albumin+ cells
protocols.start_requirements: Undifferentiated mouse ES cells (Keller-lab reporter lines were kept feeder-free and serum-free with LIF and BMP4 10 ng/ml). Dissociate to single cells and seed 2-4 × 10⁴ cells/ml in SFD medium in 60-mm low-attachment Petri dishes without growth factors.

stages.name: EB formation (no factors)
stages.base_medium: SFD serum-free differentiation medium: 75% IMDM + 25% Ham's F12, 0.5% N2 and 1% B27 (v/v), 0.05% BSA, 2 mM glutamine, 0.5 mM ascorbic acid, 4.5 × 10⁻⁴ M MTG, penicillin/streptomycin
stages.feeding: No medium change for 48 h
actions: Seed 2-4 × 10⁴ ES cells per ml in SFD in low-attachment Petri dishes
Culture 48 h without added factors
stages.checkpoint: Small uniform EBs

stages.name: Definitive endoderm induction
stages.base_medium: SFD serum-free differentiation medium: 75% IMDM + 25% Ham's F12, 0.5% N2 and 1% B27 (v/v), 0.05% BSA, 2 mM glutamine, 0.5 mM ascorbic acid, 4.5 × 10⁻⁴ M MTG, penicillin/streptomycin
stages.feeding: Single addition at re-aggregation
actions: Dissociate day-2 EBs with trypsin/EDTA
Re-aggregate at 2-6 × 10⁴ cells/ml in new Petri dishes in SFD with activin A
stages.checkpoint: c-Kit+ Cxcr4+ cells by flow (or Brachyury/Foxa2/c-Kit co-expression in reporter lines)

stages.name: Hepatic specification
stages.base_medium: SFD serum-free differentiation medium: 75% IMDM + 25% Ham's F12, 0.5% N2 and 1% B27 (v/v), 0.05% BSA, 2 mM glutamine, 0.5 mM ascorbic acid, 4.5 × 10⁻⁴ M MTG, penicillin/streptomycin

factors.name: BMP4
factors.role: Required for hepatic specification of the endoderm

stages.feeding: 2 days
actions: Dissociate EBs with trypsin/EDTA (optionally sort the c-Kit+ Cxcr4+ fraction)
Re-aggregate at high density, 5 × 10⁵ cells/ml, in 24-well low-cluster plates with BMP4, bFGF and activin A

stages.name: Hepatocyte maturation (plated)
stages.base_medium: SFD-based hepatic medium with 4.5 × 10⁻⁴ M MTG

factors.name: VEGF
factors.role: Listed for the original protocol in later papers from the same labs

actions: Plate cells on gelatin-coated dishes (2 × 10⁵ cells/ml in a restating Keller-lab paper)
Maintain in hepatic medium and analyse Afp/albumin by ICC or flow, albumin secretion and glycogen storage
stages.checkpoint: Polygonal epithelial cells positive for Afp and albumin; transcripts for Alb, Tat, Cps1, Cyp7a1 and Cyp3a11; albumin secretion and glycogen storage

materials: Low-attachment Petri dishes and 24-well low-cluster plates
Antibodies to c-Kit and Cxcr4 for flow
tips: BMP4 is the key addition: without it the activin-induced endoderm is not efficiently specified to the hepatic lineage.

c-Kit/Cxcr4 flow at the end of the activin step is the in-process control; Keller-lab reporter lines (Brachyury-GFP, Foxa2-hCD4) or the ENDM1 antibody have been used for sorting the endoderm fraction.
Later papers from the same groups use 75 ng/ml activin A from day 2 to day 5 for the endoderm step (Han 2011; Bardot 2017), so the activin dose and length of the step vary between versions.
The derived cells were shown to engraft and proliferate in injured mouse liver in the original paper.
pitfalls: The product is an immature, fetal-like hepatocyte (Afp-high); do not expect adult levels of cytochrome P450 activity.

Versions of this protocol differ on timing: one restating paper re-aggregates with BMP4/bFGF/activin at day 4 and plates at day 6, another plates on gelatin at day 5. Decide on one schedule and keep it.
Each dissociation/re-aggregation loses cells; keep trypsin exposure short and re-aggregate at the stated densities.
unverified: The Nat Biotechnol full text was not accessible; only the abstract was read. Stage timings and concentrations are taken from papers by the same authors that restate the method: Kubo et al. 2011 (PLoS One, PMID 21931641; 'Protocol #2', days 0-6: densities, activin A 50 ng/ml at day 2, BMP4 50 + bFGF 10 + activin A 50 ng/ml at day 4, plating on gelatin at day 6) and Gadue et al. 2009 (Stem Cells, PMID 19522011; plated hepatic medium with BMP4 50, TGF-α 20, bFGF 10, EGF 10, HGF 10 ng/ml, dexamethasone 10⁻⁷ M, MTG).

VEGF 10 ng/ml in the plated stage comes from Christodoulou et al. 2011 (J Clin Invest, PMID 21537085), which also uses EGF 20 and HGF 20 ng/ml and plates at day 5; VEGF is listed among the hepatic inducers of the original protocol in Han et al. 2012 (PMC4215546). The exact original doses were not confirmed.
Length of the plated maturation stage in the original paper is not confirmed; day 18 is used here because Christodoulou 2011 analysed day 18-19 cultures. Feeding interval not confirmed.
B27 with or without retinoic acid: Kubo 2011 used B27 with vitamin A; Gadue 2006 used B27 without retinoic acid. Which was used in the original was not confirmed.
The 55% / 70% / 60% efficiency figures are from the summary table in Han et al. 2012, not read from the original paper.

protocols.name: Low-serum monolayer with small molecules IDE1 or IDE2 (Borowiak 2009)
protocols.principle: Two cell-permeable small molecules found in a 4000-compound screen, IDE1 and IDE2, induce Sox17+/Foxa2+ definitive endoderm from feeder-depleted ES cells plated as a sparse monolayer in low-serum medium, replacing activin A or Nodal.

source.authors: Borowiak M, Maehr R, Chen S, et al.
source.title: Small molecules efficiently direct endodermal differentiation of mouse and human embryonic stem cells

protocols.efficiency: At day 6 of treatment 81 ± 14% (IDE1) and 76 ± 14% (IDE2) of mouse ES-derived cells were Sox17+, and over 95% of the Sox17+ cells co-expressed Foxa2; activin A gave fewer Sox17+ cells at early time points (13% at day 2, 28% at day 4)
protocols.start_requirements: Mouse ES cells grown on irradiated MEF feeders in DMEM + 15% FBS + LIF to 80-90% confluence. Deplete feeders by plating the suspension on gelatin for 30 min, then seed the ES cells at 2,500 cells/cm² on gelatinised plates and culture overnight before induction.

stages.name: Feeder depletion and seeding
stages.base_medium: Mouse ES medium (DMEM, 15% FBS, 2 mM L-glutamine, non-essential amino acids, 2-mercaptoethanol, LIF)
stages.feeding: Overnight
actions: Trypsinise ES cells and pre-plate on gelatin for 30 min to let MEFs attach
Seed the non-attached ES cells at 2,500 cells/cm² on gelatin-coated plates
Culture overnight
stages.checkpoint: Sparse, evenly spread single cells and tiny colonies

stages.name: Endoderm induction
stages.base_medium: DMEM with L-glutamine and low serum (0.2% FBS in the growth-factor arm)

factors.name: IDE1
factors.conc: 250-800 nM reported as the optimal range (EC50 125 nM); the Methods text states 5 µM

factors.name: IDE2 (alternative to IDE1)
factors.conc: 250-800 nM reported as the optimal range (EC50 223 nM); the Methods text states 5 µM

actions: Switch to low-serum differentiation medium containing IDE1 or IDE2 (use one, not both; no synergy was seen)
Treat for 6 days; Sox17+ cells peak at day 6 of treatment
Analyse Sox17 and Foxa2 by ICC or flow, or continue to pancreatic progenitor induction
stages.checkpoint: About a third of cells Sox17+ after 2 days and 40-50% after 4 days; clustered epithelial-like Sox17+ Foxa2+ cells at day 6 with few or no extra-embryonic endoderm marker-positive cells

materials: Irradiated MEF feeders and ES medium with LIF for maintenance
Optional: Wnt3a, activin A or Nodal for a growth-factor control
tips: Growth-factor control arm from the same paper: Wnt3a 25 ng/ml + activin A 50 ng/ml (or Nodal 500 ng/ml) in DMEM + L-glutamine + 0.2% FBS for 1 day, then activin A or Nodal alone in the same medium for 4-6 days.
Adding Nodal to IDE2 raised Sox17+ cells at day 4 (55.8% versus 42% with compound alone); Wnt3a added nothing, and combining IDE1 with IDE2 gave no synergy.
For pancreatic progenitors the paper then switches to DMEM + B27 with FGF10 50 ng/ml, KAAD-cyclopamine 0.75 µM and retinoic acid 2 µM (or indolactam V 330 nM) for 4 days.
A Sox17 reporter line (Sox17-dsRed in the paper) makes dose-finding quick; titrate the compound on your own line.
pitfalls: The paper is internally inconsistent on dose: the Results give 250-800 nM as the most effective non-toxic range, while the Experimental Procedures say compounds were added at 5 µM (the screening concentration). Titrate rather than assume.

Sox17 is also expressed by extra-embryonic endoderm; dispersed Sox17+ cells that co-express Gata4, Sparc, Afp or Dab2 are extra-embryonic, whereas compound-induced definitive endoderm forms clustered epithelial patches lacking those markers.
Starting density is low (2,500 cells/cm²); residual feeders or higher density change the response.
unverified: Read from the PMC author manuscript (PMC4564293), not the final published version.
Serum percentage of the medium used with IDE1/IDE2 is ambiguous: 0.2% FBS is stated for the growth-factor arm and 2% FBS for the primary screen.
Feeding interval during the 6-day treatment is not stated.
Day numbering here counts seeding as day 0, so the paper's 'day 6 of treatment' is day 7.

cell_types.notes: Activin/Nodal dose is the main lever: high activin in serum-free conditions gives endoderm, whereas low activin together with BMP4 gives mesoderm. Sox17 and Afp are both shared with extra-embryonic endoderm, which forms readily in EBs, so always use more than one marker. Hepatocyte-like cells from these protocols are fetal in character.
